message.content:
{
  "keywords": [
    "repair",
    "community",
    "tomorrow"
  ],
  "interpretation": "The act of repair is not just physical restoration but a collective, generational process where community invests in shared futures through care, patience, and collaboration.",
  "audience": "Young adults and families engaged in local civic or neighborhood initiatives",
  "objective": "To inspire action and emotional connection by showing how small, everyday acts of repair can build resilient, intergenerational communities",
  "core_message": "Tomorrow begins not with new things, but with the careful repair of what already exists—within our homes, neighborhoods, and relationships.",
  "concept": {
    "title": "Tomorrow is Built on Repair",
    "central_idea": "A single, weathered wooden house is being slowly rebuilt brick by brick, not from scratch, but by layering new materials over the old, with each new piece reflecting a different member of the community.",
    "connection_to_keywords": "The house symbolizes community; the act of layering new materials over the old represents repair; the slow, deliberate progression toward a complete structure embodies the vision of tomorrow as a future shaped by care and continuity."
  },
  "copy": {
    "headline": "Tomorrow is Built on Repair",
    "subtitle": "Each brick, each nail, each hand that returns to what’s broken—helps build a future that remembers its roots.",
    "call_to_action": "Start a repair circle in your neighborhood."
  },
  "visual_direction": {
    "main_subject": "A half-ruined wooden house being rebuilt from the inside out, with new layers of brick, wood, and fabric being added over the original structure",
    "setting": "A quiet, sun-dappled neighborhood street at golden hour",
    "visual_relationship": "The original structure remains visible and integral, showing cracks and worn edges, while the new layers grow outward in a spiral pattern, symbolizing growth through continuity",
    "supporting_elements": [
      "Faint outlines of children’s drawings on the walls",
      "A single tool (a hammer) resting on a windowsill",
      "A patch of moss growing from a cracked foundation"
    ],
    "style": "Realistic with soft, painterly textures and subtle depth",
    "mood": "Hopeful, grounded, patient"
  },
  "layout": {
    "focal_point": "The center of the house, where the new and old materials meet at a single beam",
    "composition": "Diagonal flow from the lower left (cracked foundation) to upper right (completed roof), guiding the eye through the process of repair",
    "reading_order": "Headline → subtitle → call to action, with visual journey from broken to whole",
    "typography": "Headline in bold, serif font with slight shadow; subtitle in thin, clean sans-serif; call to action in bold, slightly larger font with a soft underline"
  },
  "palette": {
    "colors": [
      "warm terracotta",
      "weathered oak brown",
      "soft sage green",
      "dusty rose",
      "sunlit gold"
    ],
    "rationale": "The warm earth tones represent the foundation of community and the passage of time. Sage green and dusty rose introduce renewal and care. Sunlit gold highlights the future, showing how repair brings light and hope."
  },
  "avoid": [
    "a list of repair items",
    "individual icons for each keyword",
    "overly abstract or symbolic imagery",
    "a future utopia with no connection to the present"
  ]
}
